records.title: Intermediate-area cylinders in the principal quadratic stratum

accepted_sections.heading: Abstract
paragraphs: Delecroix asked for the area spectrum of cylinders on large-genus square-tiled surfaces, highlighting the normalized-area window [g^(−1/2),2g^(−1/2)]. For the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum, with the number of squares tending to infinity before the genus, we derive a Poisson limit at every intermediate scale s_g→0, g s_g→∞. The rescaled cylinder areas converge to a Poisson point process of intensity dx/(2x); compact-window counts converge with every fixed joint moment. The highlighted count tends to Poisson((log2)/2), and its mean and variance have the same limit. The proof extracts a uniform Gamma/Dirichlet approximation from the published formulas of Delecroix–Liu and Delecroix–Goujard–Zograf–Zorich, then applies classical assembly identities and elementary tail estimates. The weighted permutation model and its unmarked Poisson approximation are prior results. We explicitly credit the earlier microscopic announcements and retain their unresolved normalization discrepancy with the short problem report. AI tools were used extensively; no external human peer review is asserted.

accepted_sections.heading: The idea in plain English
paragraphs: Square-tiled surfaces split into maximal horizontal cylinders. This paper studies the fraction of the total surface area occupied by each cylinder in the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum.

First fix the genus and let the maximum number of squares tend to infinity. Then let the genus grow. At every shrinking area scale that is still large compared with the reciprocal genus, the geometric cylinder-area counts have a Poisson limit.

The conclusion includes the whole rescaled point process and every fixed joint moment of counts in finitely many disjoint compact windows. It is stronger than only identifying the mean in one highlighted window.

accepted_sections.heading: The precise result
paragraphs: Fix g≥2. Sample uniformly from isomorphism classes of square-tiled half-translation surfaces in Q(1^(4g−4)) made from at most N unit squares, allow all positive cylinder heights, count each maximal horizontal cylinder once, and divide its area by total surface area. First N→∞ gives the law ν_g; the customary automorphism weighting gives the same fixed-genus limit. Only afterward does g→∞.

For every deterministic positive s_g with s_g→0 and g*s_g→∞, the actual geometric point measure Σ_i δ_(X_i/s_g) converges vaguely on (0,∞) to PPP(dx/(2x)). This is the marked normalized-area process, not only the auxiliary unmarked component model.

For any fixed finite family of pairwise disjoint compact intervals [a_l,b_l]⊂(0,∞), the counts converge jointly to independent Poisson variables with means (1/2)log(b_l/a_l), and every fixed joint moment converges.

The count in [g^(−1/2),2g^(−1/2)] converges to Poisson((log2)/2); its mean and variance tend to (log2)/2, and its zero-count probability tends to 2^(−1/2). The vertical marginal has the same law by symmetry.

accepted_sections.heading: Why the result holds
paragraphs: Published geometric graph formulas give a uniform comparison with the prior weighted-permutation law a_j=ζ(2j)/(2j). Its area marks are normalized independent Gamma variables, conditionally giving a Dirichlet vector.

Classical assembly identities give the unmarked intermediate-window law. An expected weighted Gamma-mark error, split across small, intermediate and large component sizes, vanishes even when g*s_g tends to infinity arbitrarily slowly.

Concentration of the total Gamma mass gives the normalized-area process. Uniform bounds on higher compact-window count moments, a uniform good-event density comparison and negligible exceptional moments transfer every fixed joint moment to the geometry; total variation alone is not used to transfer unbounded expectations.

accepted_sections.heading: Scope and limitations
paragraphs: The theorem concerns the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum with the square-count limit before the genus. It supplies neither a diagonal N(g) limit, arbitrary-stratum extension nor a simultaneous all-direction statement on one surface.

The microscopic regime g*s_g=O(1), the macroscopic regime s_g of order1 and relative accuracy for arbitrary rare events are outside the result. The statement addresses intermediate areas rather than every meaning of a full area spectrum.

The exact Gamma total and Liu’s thesis use 6g−6, while the short problem report prints 4g−4. These give different fixed microscopic laws and remain distinct; the paper makes no new microscopic theorem or correction of that report.

Delecroix–Liu’s earlier microscopic announcements, Liu’s all-multiplicity thesis law and the primitive conjectural slide version are prior intellectual contributions. The complete announced project may contain additional overlapping results; its contents and priority remain uncertain. No first-priority or continued-open-status claim is made.

The established geometric formulas and uniform intersection-number estimates, exact weighted model, selected-component identity and classical unmarked Poisson approximation receive prior credit. The contribution here is the explicit geometric comparison, Gamma-marking transfer and all-fixed-moment consequence.

records.title: Irreducibility of exposed-point varieties of discotopes

accepted_sections.heading: Abstract
paragraphs: We prove that the complex Zariski closure of the exposed points of any finite Minkowski sum of ellipsoidal discs of dimension at least two is irreducible. No genericity or full-dimensionality assumption is needed. This proves the exposed-point irreducibility conjecture stated by Meroni in the 2023 Oberwolfach report. Under an explicit generic condition on the summand spans, we also prove that this closure equals the purely nonlinear part defined by Gesmundo and Meroni, thereby proving their 2022 irreducibility conjecture. The proof uses a connected real-analytic support-point parametrization. A nongeneric example shows why the two varieties must be distinguished.

accepted_sections.heading: The idea in plain English
paragraphs: A discotope is formed by adding centered ellipsoidal balls, which may lie in different linear subspaces. A point is exposed if one nonzero real linear functional has that point as its unique maximizer.

The paper proves that the complex algebraic closure of all exposed points is irreducible whenever every summand has dimension at least two. The conclusion covers arbitrary configurations, including repeated discs and sums lying in a smaller ambient span.

The earlier purely nonlinear part is a different algebraic set. The paper proves equality with the exposed-point closure under an explicit generic-position condition and gives a nongeneric example where equality fails.

accepted_sections.heading: The precise result
paragraphs: For every finite positive sum D=D_1+⋯+D_N⊂R^d of centered ellipsoidal balls whose actual span dimensions are all at least two, E(D)=Zar_C(Exp(D)) is irreducible over C. Exp(D) is the actual set of unique maximizers of nonzero real linear functionals. No genericity or full-dimensionality assumption is required.

Separately, suppose D is full-dimensional and every subset J of summand spans L_i satisfies dim(Σ_(i∈J)L_i)=min(d,Σ_(i∈J)dim L_i). Then S(D)=E(D), where S(D)=Zar_C[(Σ_i ∂_(L_i)D_i)∩∂D] uses the relative boundary in each summand span. Thus S(D) is irreducible under this explicit GP condition.

For every feasible prescribed full-rank summand type, GP is a nonempty real Zariski-open condition. Distinct Vandermonde columns witness every subset rank simultaneously. As in the earlier discotope work, the total span may be used as the ambient space.

Outside generic position, S(D) can strictly contain E(D). Two identical unit xy-discs plus one unit xz-disc give e_3∈S(D) while a polynomial vanishing on E(D) has value 16 at e_3. The separate equality theorem is therefore essential to the earlier S-conjecture application.

accepted_sections.heading: Why the result holds
paragraphs: Write D_i=A_i(B^(m_i)) with A_i injective. The normal u gives a unique summand support point precisely when A_i^T u≠0, with point A_i A_i^T u/||A_i^T u||. Exposed faces add, so the actual exposed-point set is exactly the image of their summed support map on the complement of the kernels.

Every excluded kernel has codimension at least two, so a two-segment detour makes the real normal domain connected. Positive real radicands make the support map real analytic without a global complex square-root branch.

If a product of two complex polynomials vanishes on the analytic image, one factor vanishes on a nonempty open part of the domain. Analytic uniqueness then forces that factor to vanish throughout the connected domain. The complex vanishing ideal is prime and the closure irreducible.

For S=E, a supporting normal kills a subset of summand spans. GP forces those spans to form a direct sum inside its perpendicular hyperplane. Their joint transpose is onto, allowing one normal perturbation to realize all prescribed unit relative-boundary parameters simultaneously. The resulting exposed points converge to the original boundary sum.

accepted_sections.heading: Scope and limitations
paragraphs: The general theorem assumes each summand has actual dimension at least two. A rank-one interval has two exposed points, and a planar disc plus a nonzero segment has two distinct conic components, so rank-one summands cannot be included indiscriminately.

Equality S=E is asserted under full dimensionality and the every-subset GP condition, with explicit ambient-span reduction. It is not asserted for arbitrary nongeneric sums; the repeated-disc example separates the two varieties algebraically.

The paper establishes no degree formula, birationality statement or irreducibility of the entire complex critical locus. General convex summands, infinite sums and other scope extensions are not part of its theorem.

The connected analytic-image principle, support-gradient parametrization and known discotope special cases are prior work. The contribution is their unrestricted exposed-point application and the generic identification bridge. Historical first priority and current worldwide open status are not asserted.

list_items: F. Gesmundo and C. Meroni, The Geometry of Discotopes, Le Matematiche 77(1) (2022), 143–171: Definition 3.3 and Conjecture 8.2 concern S. Theorems 4.3/6.1 establish generic low boundary-dimension-sum and rank-two cases; Remark 3.4 covers all full-dimensional summands. Section 5 already uses support gradients; Section 2 gives bases genericity and ambient-span reduction.

W. Kucharz and K. Kurdyka, Rationality of semialgebraic functions, Analytic and Algebraic Geometry 2, Łódź University Press, 2017, 85–96: Proof of Proposition 4.3, p.95 explicitly records the real-Zariski connected analytic-image principle. The manuscript supplies the complex-coefficient prime-ideal argument.

C. Meroni, Two convex conjectures for different flavours, New Directions in Real Algebraic Geometry, OWR 20 (2023), Report 15/2023, 829–832: Conjecture 1, p.830 defines the exposed-point closure E and asks its irreducibility for generic discotopes with all summands of dimension at least two. The first theorem removes genericity.
